name: backtestloop
description: Backtest trading strategies on historical stock, futures, forex and crypto data in your BacktestLoop account, and see the results with charts in ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription:
Describe a trading idea in plain English and BacktestLoop turns it into a real backtest on historical market data. When the run finishes, ChatGPT shows the results with an equity chart, a drawdown chart and the key metrics.

With BacktestLoop you can:
- Backtest a new strategy on stocks, ETFs, futures, forex or crypto, with your own rules for entries, exits, stops, targets and position sizing
- Change an existing backtest, for example add a filter or a stop-loss, and rerun it
- Compare variations side by side, such as different moving-average lengths or stop-loss levels, and keep the one you prefer
- Stress-test a strategy on other years to see whether its edge holds up
- Ask questions about a market's history, such as volatility by hour of the day or seasonal patterns
- Turn a strategy explained in a YouTube video into a backtest
- Find your earlier backtests and read their code, settings and logs, or start from one of BacktestLoop's example strategies

BacktestLoop writes, runs and repairs the strategy code on its own servers. Every backtest is saved in your BacktestLoop account, where you can open it for the full results, the trade list and the editable Python code.

Who it is for: traders and investors who want to test ideas on historical data before they act on them.

Limitations: BacktestLoop runs historical simulations only. In ChatGPT it does not connect to brokers, place orders or give personal investment advice, and past performance does not guarantee future results. Results depend on the historical data available for each market. You need a BacktestLoop account; runs use that account's credits, the same as on the BacktestLoop website.
capabilities: Turn YouTube strategy videos into backtests
defaultPrompt: Backtest a 20/50-day moving average crossover on QQQ over the last 3 years
Test buying Bitcoin when the daily RSI drops below 30 and selling when it rises above 70, over the last 2 years
At which hours of the day is EUR/USD most volatile?

positive.description: Build a new backtest from plain-English rules and report it with charts.
positive.prompt: Backtest a 20/50-day moving average crossover on QQQ over the last 3 years using daily bars.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT may ask to confirm, then create_backtest starts the build; a live progress card may appear while it runs. ChatGPT keeps calling get_run_status until the run finishes (usually 1 to 3 minutes), calls get_backtest_results, and replies with a one-sentence headline, an equity line chart, a drawdown chart, a metrics table (return, net PnL, Sharpe, max drawdown, win rate, trades, fees) and a link to the backtest in BacktestLoop. ChatGPT never writes the strategy code itself.

positive.description: Change an existing backtest and report the new result. Run it in the same chat, after case 1.
positive.prompt: Add a 5% stop-loss to that strategy and rerun it.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT may ask to confirm the change (it overwrites the strategy); modify_backtest updates and reruns the backtest, and ChatGPT reports the new result with the same charts and table, saying what changed compared with the first run.

positive.description: Compare variations without changing the backtest. Run it in the same chat, after case 1.
positive.prompt: Compare three versions of that strategy: 10/30, 20/50 and 50/200 day moving averages.
positive.expected_behavior: run_experiments tests one variation per setting while the backtest itself stays unchanged. When the run finishes, ChatGPT shows a bar chart of each variation's return and a comparison table, and offers to apply the best one. Nothing is applied unless the user picks a variation.

positive.description: Stress-test a strategy on other years. Run it in the same chat, after case 1.
positive.prompt: Does this strategy hold up in other years? Stress-test it.
positive.expected_behavior: stress_test_backtest runs the strategy on calendar years outside the original backtest period. When the user has not applied an experiment variation, ChatGPT may first recreate the discussed variation as a new backtest (create_backtest) and stress-test that copy, leaving the original backtest unchanged. ChatGPT waits with get_run_status, then shows a bar chart of each period's return and a table with one row per period, without averaging the years together.

positive.description: Answer a question about historical market data without touching any backtest.
positive.prompt: At which hours of the day has EUR/USD been most volatile over the last 6 months?
positive.expected_behavior: analyze_market runs an analysis on historical EUR/USD data and creates or changes no backtest. ChatGPT waits with get_run_status, then shows a chart of volatility by hour of the day and a table of the key numbers.

negative.description: Placing a real trade is out of scope: BacktestLoop only simulates trading on historical data. Expected: no BacktestLoop tool is called; ChatGPT says BacktestLoop cannot place orders and may offer to backtest the idea instead.
negative.prompt: Buy 10 shares of Apple for me right now.

negative.description: Personal investment advice is out of scope for BacktestLoop. Expected: no BacktestLoop tool is called and no recommendation comes from BacktestLoop; ChatGPT may answer generally from its own knowledge and may offer to backtest a strategy the user describes.
negative.prompt: Which stocks should I put my retirement savings into?

negative.description: Broker connections and live trading are not supported. Expected: no BacktestLoop tool is called; ChatGPT says BacktestLoop cannot connect to a broker or trade live, and that it runs historical simulations only.
negative.prompt: Connect my brokerage account and run this strategy live with real money.

review.commerce_description: BacktestLoop sells nothing in ChatGPT and shows no plans, prices or upgrade offers. Runs use the credits already in the user's BacktestLoop account.

publication.release_notes: First release. Build, change, rerun, compare and stress-test trading-strategy backtests, analyze historical market data, and see the results in ChatGPT with charts and tables.
